post.description:
"Is a guest" is decided from the markers guest-register creates:
the mob-source `external_user_links` row proves the account was
minted for a MOB device, and `is_temporary` (still true) proves it
has not been upgraded yet — this method zeroes it, the same flag
User::completeRegistration zeroes for the core signup flow. No new
column, no reliance on the incidental `@guest.local` email pattern.

Token rotation: EVERY prior bearer for the user is revoked (the
calling one included — guest-register mints a fresh bearer per call,
so several may be live) and one new token is minted with the same
`subproject:{id}` ability stamping generateAuthDataForUser applies
(both funnel through subprojectTokenAbilities).

Conflict semantics follow the Deals controllers: a caller that is
not an un-upgraded MOB guest gets 409 CONFLICT. Email collisions are
a 422 from MobUpgradeRequest's `unique:users,email` rule.

GET /api/deal/{guid}/dispatch[?host=<host>&to_system=<sub>]

Anonymous by design (mirrors /status): the visitor holds only the guid.
The host defaults to `?host=`, then the X-Domain header, then the
request host. Returns `{guid, tenant, status, outcome, next:{surface,
host, url, kind}}`; 404 when the guid resolves to no deal.

It does NOT resolve "who governs" — the governing body ({leader,
officials}) is the sibling resolver's job (§4).

get.description:
Same `after_seq` sequence cursor as the member endpoint
(DealWizardController::events), but with a STRICT non-sensitive
projection: deal_events payloads carry intake content —
`deal.created` ships the raw problem statement, `deal.info_collected`
ships answer_keys, `deal.step.completed` ships full step results —
so the public feed whitelists {sequence, event_type, created_at}
and adds only the routing-relevant {from, to} pair on
`deal.state.*` rows. The payload column is NEVER serialized here
(epic risk 7: public vs member payload split). Never reuse the
member DealResource (it includes `problem`) on this surface.

The guid IS the Deal primary key (PipelineDealActivator vends
`deal_guid => $deal->id`). Resolution bypasses the subproject
global scope because the visitor is anonymous and carries no
X-Domain context — cross-tenant by design, mirroring status().

Tenancy (epic risk 9): the SubprojectScoped global scope is strict
equality, which would hide legacy deals whose subproject_id was
never backfilled — drop it and apply `subproject_id = ctx OR IS

preserves cross-tenant isolation once the scope is gone.

The created_at cutoff (config deals.active_sessions_cutoff,
epic risk 11) fences off the ~142 pre-projection prod zombies
(all parked in `analyzing`) so they never resurface as resume
cards. `active` defaults to true — the app always sends
?active=1; pass active=0 to include completed/failed history.

post.description:
The approval is recorded as an IntakeApprovalStep row
({selected_asset_id, selected_asset, approved_at}), the pause flag is
cleared, and the pipeline is RESUMED via the canonical HITL-resume
dispatch (PipelineBasedProgramCreationJob, the same pattern as
PipelineStateFinishedStep::saveFollowupQuestionAnswer). On the resumed
run the already-passed steps skip and the remaining catalog steps
(PublicEvidenceEnrichment → ConfidenceLabel →
StudentSignalToTicketStep) execute; StudentSignalToTicketStep::
selectAsset() consumes the recorded IntakeApprovalStep pick to create
the work order.

  401 — unauthenticated (route middleware)
  404 — kill switch off, unknown signal id, a signal belonging to
        another tenant, OR a pipeline_states pause that is NOT a
        facilities intake signal (no structuring row under either
        StructuredObservationPayload step name — e.g. a codify-wizard
        GenerateFollowUpQuestions pause). All indistinguishable by
        design.
  409 — signal exists but is not awaiting intake approval
  422 — asset_id missing, not among the LinkAssetStep candidates, or
        the signal has NO recorded candidates at all (fail closed:
        nothing to pick from means nothing is approvable)

Concurrency: the awaiting-check + record + clear run in one DB
transaction with the pipeline_states row locked FOR UPDATE, so two
racing approves serialize — the loser re-reads the cleared flag and
gets the 409, never a second IntakeApprovalStep row.

post.description:
Reaching `executive_action` (coarse 'enacted') is the draft→effective
flip — the ONLY such path on the lighting route until the ballot HTTP
surface (G4) exists:
  - published_at is stamped (enactment implies publication, #281
    decision 4), so the row leaves the queue (membership rule above);
  - each of the draft's PENDING typed parameter proposals (its own
    policy_parameters rows' latest version with effective_at NULL and
    superseded_at NULL) is made effective via
    PolicyParameterService::setEffective(source='review_promoted') —
    the existing WS-A/W-H spine primitive, which appends the effective
    version, repoints effective_version_id and dispatches PolicyChanged
    (CHANGE_PARAMETER_SET → DeliverPolicyWebhookJob fan-out);
  - one policy-level PolicyChanged (CHANGE_UPDATED) announces the
    publication itself.
NOTE: proposals filed against ANOTHER policy's live knob (propose()
never repoints an existing parameter's policy_id) are not flipped here
— only parameters belonging to the draft are; the original proposal
version rows are retained untouched as the review trail.

Mid-ladder promotes touch nothing public: no publication, no effective
values, no PolicyChanged — just the status write.

in OUTCOME_VERIFICATION_PLAN.md §4: `{rollout_id, rubric_item_id, weight,

against CI-RLHF's Idempotency-Key for the full TTL. Unknown-rollout is a
TEMPORAL condition, checked in-service after the controller replay

The rules here reject only deterministic failures, which are safe to
cache-replay.

StorePolicyDraftRequest.description:
WS5 (codify-launch#283) — payload shape for POST /api/internal/policy-drafts.

Auth and the `m2m:services` Sanctum ability are gated upstream by route
middleware; the per-tenant `policy:draft:<tld>` ability binding is enforced
in the controller AFTER the target subproject resolves (403, not 422).
`authorize()` therefore returns true, keeping the default Laravel 422
`{message, errors}` response for assertJsonValidationErrors().

The ACTOR is server-derived (AgentPolicyActorResolver) — on the native
shape every client-supplied actor/authorship/state field is `prohibited`
so the endpoint can never be talked into minting an identity or skipping
the review state.

WS5 (codify-launch#286, golden-fixture parity with the agt #284 drafting
tool): the endpoint ALSO accepts the `policy_draft.v1` contract envelope
(schemas/policy/v1/policy_draft.v1.json — `contract: "policy_draft"`,
`version: "1"`). prepareForValidation() translates it onto the native
shape: `tld` resolves the target subproject (codify.<tld> apex domain or
the stamped codify_tld_override; no first-label fallback — unresolvable
tld ⇒ subproject_id missing ⇒ 422) and `parameters[].proposed_value`
maps to `value`. The envelope's `actor_ref` is REQUIRED by the agt schema
(the bearer token identifies agt the service, not the acting PDA) but is
NEVER TRUSTED: it must equal the schema-pinned `pda:codify.<tld>` shape
for the payload's own tld, and the PERSISTED actor is still derived
server-side from the token + claw registry exactly as on the native path
(a provisioned city-tier claw records pda:codify.city, not the envelope's
pda:codify.nyc). On the native shape `actor_ref` stays prohibited.

m2m tokens are cross-tenant by convention, so the target tenant
comes explicitly in the payload (validated against the token's
per-tenant policy:draft:<tld> ability in the controller).

VoiceInterpretRequest.description:
POST /api/public/voice/interpret — guest voice utterance upload.

Guest endpoint: authorize() is unconditionally true; tenancy is enforced
upstream by SetDomainContext (X-Tenant-Domain / X-Domain).

The mimetypes list is MediaRecorder-real, not spec-pure: Chrome emits
audio/webm (finfo often sniffs the EBML container as video/webm),
Safari emits audio/mp4 (sniffed as video/mp4 or audio/x-m4a), Firefox
emits audio/ogg, and libmagic reports WAV as audio/x-wav. `mimetypes`
validates the sniffed content type, so the sniffed variants are
load-bearing, not belt-and-braces.
